stories.title: Exploring sex differences in how the brain adapts to overeating
stories.summary: Overeating alters neural pathways involved in feeding and metabolism, but how fast do these adaptive changes occur? And do these adaptations occur similarly in males and females?

stories.title: After adult-onset hearing loss, an adaptation in the brain may improve vision
stories.summary: To adapt to changing environments and bodily functions across the life span, many mammals rely on compensatory changes in the brain. One major change as mammals age is that individual senses, such as hearing or vision, can be weakened or lost.

stories.title: Enhancing the cell's natural recycling center improves Alzheimer's features in animal models
stories.summary: A defining feature of Alzheimer's disease is the abnormal, sustained accumulation of protein aggregates such as tau inside brain cells, which disrupts the cells' normal functions.

stories.title: They Tried Kratom for Its Health Benefits, Then They Became Addicted

stories.title: Overtraining may disrupt the brain's dopamine regulation, leaving levels elevated during rest

stories.title: Could consciousness begin deep in the brain? Researchers make the case
stories.summary: Close your eyes and cover your ears. Much of the world around you disappears from view and hearing, yet your sense of being present, of being conscious, remains. What creates that basic feeling of being "you"?

stories.title: In parallel mouse studies, researchers fail to replicate many reported effects of psilocybin
stories.summary: Experimental trials of psychedelic drugs in both humans and animals have produced conflicting results, creating doubts about whether hallucinogens have a therapeutic role in treating neurologic or behavioral disorders such as depression and PTSD.

stories.summary: Spread through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, dengue is a viral infection that can cause anything from mild fever, flu-like symptoms and joint pain to a severe form known as dengue hemorrhagic fever.

stories.title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think

stories.title: Simple exercises and workplace changes may help Florida landscape workers manage back pain
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands of nursery and landscape workers in Florida knuckle through low back pain daily, putting them at risk for chronic discomfort, injuries and job loss.

stories.title: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a remarkable new electronic implant that could transform type 2 diabetes treatment by lowering blood sugar without insulin or traditional drugs.

stories.title: Cholesterol transport protein emerges as possible target for Parkinson's treatment
stories.summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative condition that causes the progressive loss of dopamine-producing neurons in a brain region called the substantia nigra. Its characteristic symptoms include tremors, slowed movements, rigid muscles and difficulties with balance.

stories.title: Scientists discover that some “unhealthy” diets can boost cancer immunotherapy in mice
stories.summary: In a surprising discovery, scientists found that certain diets associated with obesity can make cancer immunotherapy more effective in mice, challenging traditional assumptions about diet and cancer treatment.

stories.summary: Relying on technology can make us forgetful, but there are some simple ways to sharpen your recall. Memory experts describe the tricks and habits that can help Memory can worsen as we age, but it is often possible to do something about it.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden driver of high cholesterol and a way to stop it
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden mechanism that allows high-cholesterol diets to undermine the body's natural cholesterol defenses, and blocking it dramatically lowered harmful LDL cholesterol in mice.

stories.title: A surprising vitamin A discovery is changing what scientists know about vision
stories.summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins University have uncovered a surprising process that helps humans develop sharp vision before birth, challenging decades of assumptions about how the eye forms.

stories.title: Living alone riskier for young and middle-aged adults than seniors, study indicates
stories.summary: Loneliness has been considered a major health risk for seniors, but a new study suggests younger adults might fare even worse from living by themselves.

stories.title: Dietary Lecithin Linked to Lower Cognitive Impairment
stories.summary: Can everyday dietary lecithin defend against memory loss? stories.title: Not all antihistamines are the same—and some may affect your brain more than you think
stories.summary: Millions of people take antihistamines for allergies, but some of these medicines can make you sleepy, slow your reactions and affect your concentration. Others are much less likely to have these effects.

stories.title: Can creatine help your mental health? Here's what the latest evidence says
stories.summary: Once a supplement favored mainly by fitness fanatics, creatine has quickly become one of the most widely used dietary add-ons in the world.

stories.title: Post-COVID syndrome: Prednisolone shows modest, short-lived lift in treatment trial
stories.summary: Persistent fatigue, shortness of breath, difficulty concentrating, anxiety or low mood: Many people continue to suffer from symptoms months after a COVID-19 infection, significantly restricting their daily lives. However, reliable data on which treatments are effective remain scarce.

stories.title: FDA again bypasses advisers to remove black-box warnings from menopause treatments

stories.summary: There is not enough evidence to determine whether testosterone helps with thinking and memory in midlife women, even though it is often prescribed in the UK, according to a UCL study.

stories.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months
stories.summary: A promising new study suggests that more than half of younger adults with type 2 diabetes could achieve remission in just six months through a combination of a low-calorie diet and structured exercise.

stories.title: Cholesterol-sharing mechanism points to potential new target for pancreatic cancer treatment
stories.summary: Fox Chase Cancer Center researchers identified a potential therapeutic target for pancreatic cancer after showing that tumor growth can be slowed and immune suppression can be reduced in preclinical trials by blocking a particular protein, called anoctamin 6 (ANO6).

stories.title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you
stories.summary: Parts of plants that are usually wasted, from kiwi skin to squash seeds, contain more fibre than the parts of the plant we do eat

stories.title: Many women have never discussed heart health with a clinician, and most report multiple symptoms
stories.summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, and the risk rises during the menopause years. But an international study has revealed that only half of women know this. Many have never talked about their heart with a doctor or a nurse, and the majority are living with multiple symptoms.

stories.summary: A surprising discovery at UC San Diego suggests that chronic lower back pain may become deeply embedded in the brain's sense of personal identity.

stories.title: The parts of fruits and vegetables most throw away could save your health—and the planet
stories.summary: Most of us routinely discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at mealtime. But new research from King's College London suggests these scraps could be a valuable—and overlooked—source of dietary fiber, offering potential benefits for both public health and the environment.

stories.title: Manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, say UK experts
stories.summary: Report calls for an effort to tackle harms in similar way to obesity and smoking, and stresses need to ‘offer boys something better’ The manosphere and online misogyny should be treated by the government as a public health issue, in the same way as obesity or smoking, experts have said.

stories.title: Could a few bad dietary choices worsen your next immune response?
stories.summary: Scientists have long known that diet shapes the immune system. Now, a UC San Francisco team has found that even a brief dietary change can substantially change how the body responds to skin irritation, at least in mice.

stories.title: When things go bump in the night: How our brains trick us into hearing things that aren't there
stories.summary: It's 3 a.m. You've woken from a dead sleep because you've heard a thud in the darkness or a floorboard creaking downstairs. Or perhaps you've woken because you have the unmistakable sensation you're not alone.

stories.title: Tumor mutations and immune activity may reveal who benefits from investigational lymphoma drug
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba conducted a physician-initiated phase 2 clinical trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T-follicular helper cell lymphoma (TFHL), an aggressive and difficult-to-treat blood cancer.

stories.title: Heat waves and pollution increase stroke risk in older adults, study finds
stories.summary: A study conducted in Brazil by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) found that each additional day spent under a heat wave in São Paulo is associated with an increased risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older.

stories.title: New Transporter Bypasses Blood-Brain Barrier to Deliver Creatine
stories.summary: How can drugs bypass the brain's tightest security checkpoint? Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland discovered that hijacking the sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter (SMVT) allows creatine derivatives to cross the blood-brain barrier, offering hope for rare deficiency syndromes.

stories.title: Healthy diet may lower heart disease risk after cancer
stories.summary: Eating a healthy diet is associated with a reduced risk of heart disease and death among cancer survivors, according to a study published today in JACC: Advances.

stories.title: Antibody candidate could help preserve appetite and muscle strength in patients with cancer
stories.summary: In cancer cachexia, patients continue to lose weight, muscle and fat even when they eat. A KAIST research team has developed a therapeutic candidate that blocks a signal responsible for appetite suppression, weight loss and excessive energy expenditure.

stories.title: STI screening linked to fewer preterm births
stories.summary: Screening and treating pregnant patients for three common sexually transmitted infections (STIs) twice during pregnancy was associated with a 23% lower risk of preterm birth compared with standard care, according to a randomized clinical trial published in Clinical Infectious Diseases from…

stories.title: Vitamin-carrying protein pathway shows promise for brain drug delivery
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland have identified a transporter protein with the potential to open new avenues for improving creatine delivery into the brain and for developing other therapies targeting the central nervous system.

stories.title: These Patients Struggle With Runaway Bones. Finally There’s Hope.
stories.summary: F.O.P., a rare genetic condition, causes uncontrolled explosions of bone. A new drug may slow or halt the process.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging

stories.title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered a small group of brain cells that prevents dangerous blood pressure swings, even when average readings appear normal. The finding reveals a hidden source of cardiovascular risk and could open the door to new treatments that protect the heart and brain.

stories.title: Red meat nutrient may amp up inflammation
stories.summary: A nutrient abundant in red meat and commonly used in exercise supplements may amplify inflammation.

stories.title: Breathing “Thin Air” May Protect Against Parkinson’s
stories.summary: Can breathing thin mountain air help Parkinson's patients? Researchers demonstrated that 39 minutes of controlled intermittent hypoxia safely lowers stress hormones, raises anti-inflammatory adiponectin, and protects BDNF levels without disturbing sleep.

stories.title: Brain Disease Is Pervasive in N.F.L., New Estimate Suggests

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden reason why muscles weaken with age

stories.title: ‘Ferritin face’: are social media claims about iron deficiency fact – or fiction?

stories.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength

stories.title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut

stories.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.

stories.title: The surprisingly simple exercise that could lower your blood pressure
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple exercise routine could help lower blood pressure without requiring daily workouts or expensive equipment.

stories.title: Exercise doesn't just strengthen your heart. It rewires it
stories.summary: Regular exercise does more than strengthen the heart. New research reveals that it actually reshapes the nerves controlling how the heart functions, and the changes are surprisingly different on the left and right sides of the body.

stories.title: Scientists reveal the hidden danger of missing blood pressure medication
stories.summary: Missing blood pressure medication could mean losing much of its protection against heart attacks and strokes, according to an analysis of more than 91,000 people.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
stories.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.

stories.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side

stories.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging.

stories.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
stories.summary: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure. In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s

stories.title: Coffee calories have jumped nearly 40%. Sugar isn't the biggest culprit

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles

stories.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

stories.title: Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
stories.summary: A new Penn State study suggests that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults.

stories.summary: A study by DZNE finds that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging—and that there is more than one way to eat healthily.

stories.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage.

stories.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
stories.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
stories.summary: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers.

stories.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
stories.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early…

stories.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
stories.summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light. The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

stories.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

stories.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
stories.summary: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical…

stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
stories.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.

stories.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
stories.summary: Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months.

stories.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.

stories.title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a potential new drug can reverse severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and blocking harmful substances from reaching the liver.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.

stories.title: Yale scientists discover how stress changes the brain to make memories stronger
stories.summary: Yale scientists have uncovered how the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories.

stories.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. stories.title: Menopause is a biological transition that’s become a lucrative consumer business
stories.summary: While menopause media coverage helps to bust taboos, it also fosters a lucrative, social media and business-driven market that takes advantage of woman’s need for support.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
stories.summary: Popular diabetes and weight loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss.

stories.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength
stories.summary: A 47-year study has uncovered a surprising turning point in physical aging: fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among people who exercise regularly.

stories.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults, and scientists can't fully explain why
stories.summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved.

stories.title: Decade-long gym steroids study shows just what happens to men's hearts
stories.summary: One of the first long-term studies that followed weight-training middle-aged men for nearly a decade has found that consistent use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) leads to the thickening of the heart’s left ventricular wall, which increasingly reduces the organ's ability to function.

stories.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
stories.summary: Ice baths, massages, compression garments, and recovery supplements promise faster muscle recovery, but research suggests their benefits are often overstated, and some techniques may even undermine long-term gains.

stories.title: Scientists discover how harmful “zombie cells” hide from the immune system
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a protein that may help harmful aging cells hide from the immune system, allowing them to accumulate and fuel age-related health problems.

stories.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
stories.summary: Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological…

stories.title: After 30 years, scientists finally have a drug for a deadly brain disease
stories.summary: The FDA has approved the first drug that directly targets Alexander disease, a devastating neurological disorder affecting fewer than one in a million people.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden problem with endless smartphone scrolling
stories.summary: Excessive smartphone use may be taking a hidden toll on the brain and body, with heavy scrolling linked to poorer memory, reduced attention, disrupted sleep, and potential balance problems.

stories.title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
stories.summary: Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, have been linked to unexpectedly high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation, with some problems occurring several times more frequently among users.

stories.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days.

stories.title: Just 10 minutes of daily exercise could unlock deeper sleep
stories.summary: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently experienced more deep, restorative sleep, which is essential for brain recovery, memory, and emotional well-being.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.

stories.title: Eating olive oil before carbs has a surprising effect on blood sugar
stories.summary: A simple change in the order you eat your food could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists discovered that giving mice olive oil before carbohydrates slowed digestion and activated a surprising combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, even in mice with type…

stories.title: A surprisingly simple way to relieve knee arthritis pain without pills or surgery
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple change in how you walk could help relieve knee arthritis pain and even slow joint damage. In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without…

stories.title: Scientists discover 5 hidden brain patterns behind depression
stories.summary: Depression may not be one biological condition, but several distinct patterns of brain activity hiding under the same diagnosis.

stories.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat and keep muscle
stories.summary: A six-month study suggests that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) may offer older adults a powerful advantage: losing body fat while keeping their muscle.

stories.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
stories.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials.

stories.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
stories.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect.

stories.title: FDA-approved epilepsy drug may help reverse osteoarthritis damage
stories.summary: Researchers at Yale have identified a promising new approach to osteoarthritis that could do more than simply ease pain. The epilepsy drug lacosamide appears to block a protein involved in both pain signaling and cartilage destruction, helping damaged joints shift back toward repair in preclinical…

stories.title: An experimental drug kills fat cells, rather than shrinking them
stories.summary: Participants in two small trials lost dangerous fat around their internal organs. This fat is linked to health issues like diabetes and heart problems.

stories.title: Gene therapy and special goggles give some blind people limited sight
stories.summary: Optogenetics, recognized by the 2026 medicine Nobel, makes cells respond to light, including eye cells that normally relay signals to the brain.

stories.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
stories.summary: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders.

stories.title: Goodbye joint replacements? Stanford scientists found a way to regrow cartilage and stop arthritis
stories.summary: Scientists have found a surprising way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age.

stories.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
stories.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

stories.title: A few drops of this Japanese tree oil may help you sleep more soundly
stories.summary: In a small study, sleeping near the scent of Hinoki root essential oil was linked to fewer nighttime awakenings, better morning alertness, and brain-wave changes associated with smoother sleep onset.

stories.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
stories.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood.

stories.title: This common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
stories.summary: High-dose vitamin B3 is showing intriguing early promise as an addition to standard glioblastoma treatment, with 82% of patients in a small trial remaining progression-free after six months.

stories.title: Vitamin D drug may help crack pancreatic cancer’s protective shield
stories.summary: A vitamin D analog may help break down pancreatic cancer’s protective defenses, potentially making tumors more vulnerable to chemotherapy and immune attack. A small clinical trial found encouraging responses, especially in patients whose tumors had high levels of the vitamin D receptor.

stories.title: Diet drinks work as well as water for weight loss, major trial finds
stories.summary: A two-year randomized clinical trial involving 493 adults with overweight or obesity found that diet soft drinks were essentially as effective as water for long-term weight loss and weight maintenance.

stories.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
stories.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

stories.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

stories.title: Vitamin C linked to fewer deaths in blood disorder trial
stories.summary: Vitamin C may do more than support the immune system. In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C did not slow abnormal cell growth, but it was linked to favorable changes in inflammation and fewer serious complications.

stories.title: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit
stories.summary: High-risk MDS stem cells appear to have an unexpected “energy addiction,” relying far more heavily than healthy blood-forming cells on a molecule called NAD. Disrupting this energy pathway selectively weakened the cancer-driving cells, revealing a potential new target for treatment.

stories.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
stories.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.

stories.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
stories.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
stories.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins.

stories.title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
stories.summary: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging.

stories.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
stories.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites.

stories.title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs
stories.summary: Scientists resurrected antimicrobial peptides from mammals that lived millions of years ago and found that some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions.

stories.title: Resetting the body clock could help the brain recover after stroke
stories.summary: Strengthening the body’s natural daily rhythms helped mice recover after stroke by improving the brain’s waste-clearing system and reducing lingering inflammation.

stories.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
stories.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia.

stories.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
stories.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms.

stories.title: ‘It’s problematic’: concern as weight-loss jab maker sponsors Vogue World event
stories.summary: Critics say partnership between Mounjaro maker Eli Lilly and fashion giant suggests thinness is an aspiration The fifth iteration of Vogue World , overseen by Anna Wintour, took place in Milan on Tuesday night.

stories.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
stories.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops.

stories.title: Aging muscles may be losing strength for a reason scientists missed
stories.summary: A newly identified breakdown in communication between nerves and muscles could help explain why people lose strength as they age. Researchers were able to improve muscle strength in an animal model by targeting a key protein, raising hopes that some age-related weakness could eventually be treated.

stories.title: Breakthrough drug reverses skin aging and dramatically speeds healing
stories.summary: A topical drug that removes aging, damaged cells helped older mice heal skin wounds significantly faster. The treatment appeared to reactivate repair pathways involved in inflammation, collagen production, and new blood vessel growth.

stories.title: This new drug could break cancer’s resistance to treatment
stories.summary: A new experimental drug called CS18 may help break through cancer drug resistance by disabling several of the defenses tumors use to survive treatment. It strengthened existing therapies, restored drug sensitivity in resistant lung cancer cells, and slowed tumor growth in animal models.

stories.title: Coffee doesn’t have to keep you awake to disrupt your sleep
stories.summary: Caffeine may make sleep less restorative even when you fall asleep normally and stay in bed for eight hours, with EEG recordings revealing fewer of the slow brain waves associated with deep sleep.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal a possible cause of long COVID fatigue and brain fog
stories.summary: Researchers have found evidence that long COVID may damage dopamine releasing neurons in the brain, potentially explaining persistent fatigue, low motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties. The discovery could lead to new treatments that target the brain's dopamine system.

stories.title: Scientists create a needle-thin brain implant that can do three jobs at once
stories.summary: A new needle-thin brain implant can record neural activity, deliver drugs, and stimulate multiple brain regions using a single flexible fiber.

stories.title: Millions take calcium and vitamin D for bone health. A major review finds little benefit
stories.summary: A sweeping review of more than 153,000 adults found that calcium and vitamin D supplements, alone or together, do little to prevent fractures or falls in most older people.

stories.title: Scientists restore a brain protein and reverse signs of aging in mice
stories.summary: Scientists found that declining levels of the brain protein Menin may help drive aging, with lower levels in mice linked to inflammation, cognitive decline, weaker bones, and thinner skin.

stories.title: This popular fermented food may help flush nanoplastics from the body
stories.summary: A kimchi-derived bacterium can bind to nanoplastics under gut-like conditions and may help carry them out of the body. In mice, the probiotic more than doubled the amount of nanoplastics detected in feces, pointing to a surprising potential use for microbes from fermented foods.

stories.title: New mesothelioma drug turns cancer’s own defenses against it
stories.summary: Scientists are testing a counterintuitive way to fight mesothelioma, an aggressive asbestos-linked cancer with few effective treatments. A new experimental mesothelioma drug kills cancer cells by disabling PRX3, an antioxidant defense that tumors use to survive intense oxidative stress.

stories.title: Scientists find the whole grain “sweet spot” for better heart health
stories.summary: Eating four to six servings of whole grains a day may deliver meaningful benefits for heart health, according to a large review of 87 clinical trials. Researchers found improvements in body weight, waist size, blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, triglycerides, and some markers of inflammation.

stories.title: Ultra-processed foods linked to hidden muscle fat that may threaten your knees
stories.summary: Eating more ultra-processed foods was linked to greater fat buildup inside thigh muscles, according to MRI scans of 615 adults at risk for knee osteoarthritis. Surprisingly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for calorie intake, physical activity, and other factors.

stories.title: Scientists reversed biological age in older adults in just 4 weeks
stories.summary: Older adults who changed the balance of fat, carbohydrates, and animal protein in their diets showed signs of reduced biological age after just four weeks. The strongest result appeared in participants eating an omnivorous, lower-fat, higher-carbohydrate diet.

stories.title: Smelling chocolate helped men complete more reps without feeling more tired
stories.summary: Simply smelling chocolate helped men complete more leg extension repetitions without making the workout feel harder, with dark chocolate producing the strongest effect. The researchers think familiar food aromas may influence appetite and motivation by making the brain anticipate eating.

stories.title: Scientists discover a major brain shift between ages 50 and 75
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered sweeping changes in how the human brain controls and organizes its genome beginning in midlife, offering new clues to why aging sharply increases the risk of Alzheimer’s and other neurodegenerative diseases.

stories.title: Nearly 10,000 patients reveal what works best for knee arthritis pain relief
stories.summary: A major analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 people suggests that some of the simplest treatments may work best for knee osteoarthritis.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden cause of high blood pressure that routine tests can miss
stories.summary: A wearable device has revealed nighttime hormone surges that may expose a frequently missed cause of high blood pressure. The discovery could help explain why primary aldosteronism often escapes standard blood tests and point toward a more accurate way to diagnose it.

stories.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
stories.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue.

stories.title: Scientists find Ozempic may slow aging itself
stories.summary: Semaglutide helped older healthy mice live longer while improving memory, muscle function, blood sugar control, and several biological signs of aging.

stories.title: Scientists discover the human heart can regrow muscle after a heart attack
stories.summary: Researchers have shown for the first time that human heart muscle cells can regrow after a heart attack. The finding overturns the idea that damaged areas of the heart are completely incapable of regeneration.

stories.title: DNA treatment cuts bad cholesterol by nearly 50% without statins
stories.summary: Researchers have designed a new DNA-based treatment that targets PCSK9, a protein closely tied to high LDL cholesterol and atherosclerosis.

stories.title: Scientists find a bone-building switch that could fight osteoporosis
stories.summary: An experimental compound called AP503 significantly strengthened bones in mice by activating GPR133, a receptor that boosts bone formation while slowing bone loss.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy may have an unexpected mental health benefit
stories.summary: Semaglutide, the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy, may have benefits that extend well beyond weight loss and diabetes. In a large Swedish study of nearly 15,000 people with bipolar disorder, its use was linked to a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization.

stories.title: Early statin use linked to 15% lower dementia risk
stories.summary: Starting statins soon after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis may do more than protect the heart. In a nationwide Danish study of more than 132,000 people, those who began statin treatment within a year of diagnosis had a 15% lower relative risk of developing dementia over 10 years compared with those…

stories.title: Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
stories.summary: A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men.

stories.title: This lifestyle program improved cognition 55% more than basic health advice
stories.summary: Older adults at risk of dementia improved their memory and thinking after following lifestyle programs combining exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, and social engagement.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden problem with this popular sugar substitute
stories.summary: Sorbitol, a sugar alcohol commonly used in sugar-free candy, gum, and other low-calorie foods, may not be as harmless as it seems. Researchers at Washington University in St.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover a seafood that can reverse signs of aging
stories.summary: A substance found in edible sea squirts appeared to reverse several signs of aging in older mice. Plasmalogen supplements improved memory and learning, strengthened connections between brain cells, reduced inflammation, and even helped the mice grow thicker, darker hair.
